fermentables.name: Apple (bittersweet cider variety)

Acid is converted to g/L at 1% = 10 g/L. The class itself is Barker's LARS classification of 1903 — malic acid below 0.45% with tannin above 0.2% — which is still the basis of the trade's nomenclature. Compiled by Andrew Lea, formerly of Long Ashton, from Bulmer's Pomona (1987) and Beech and Carr (1977); the acid figures are by alkali titration and the tannin by the Lowenthal permanganate method, on freshly expressed juice rather than finished cider.

fermentables.description: A traditional if unfashionable country-wine base. Very low sugar, moderate acid.
fermentables.usageNotes: Requires heavy chaptalisation. The result is savoury and divides opinion sharply.
fermentables.attribution: Total sugars are McCance & Widdowson's Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset 2021, food code 13-517, "Tomatoes, standard, raw": 3.0 g per 100 g. CoFID is the UK's national food composition database, published by Public Health England, and it is cited here because USDA's SR Legacy set either has no entry for this fruit or has one with carbohydrate but no sugar figure. ppg is 46 times the sugars per 100 g. CoFID publishes one standard raw tomato where USDA splits red, green and yellow, which is why USDA could not be used: this record does not say which colour it describes.
fermentables.sourceNote: CoFID backs the sugar figure and the ppg from it, and nothing else here. Brix, juice yield, titratable acidity, dominant acid, pH, pectin and tannin are not in it and are not yet sourced.

fermentables.name: Beetroot
fermentables.description: Earthy from geosmin, with a deep betalain colour and a pH high enough to be a real spoilage risk.
fermentables.usageNotes: Acidify hard. Sugar beet, the industrial relative, is the source of most European beet sugar and neutral spirit.
fermentables.attribution: Sugar is USDA FoodData Central's published total-sugars figure for Beets, raw (SR Legacy, FDC ID 169145), and ppg is 46 x that per 100 g. The citation is the data endpoint rather than the portal page, which FDC serves from a client-side router and returns 404 to anything that is not a browser.

fermentables.name: Agave Piña
fermentables.description: The sugar in raw agave is inulin, a fructose polymer that yeast cannot ferment. Cooking hydrolyses it to fructose.
fermentables.usageNotes: The whole-fruit sugar figure is zero on purpose: uncooked agave yields nothing. Roast or steam for 24–48 h first, then the juice runs 22–30 Brix.
fermentables.attribution: No source. USDA's raw agave entry is the Southwest food plant at 2.58 g sugar; the agave pina used for fermentation is cooked, which converts its inulin to fermentable sugar, and this record's 0 g raw sugar is describing that uncooked state without a citation for it.

fermentables.name: Apple Juice (pressed)
fermentables.description: Fresh-pressed or shelf-stable apple juice, ready to pitch. 12 Brix works out around 1.048.
fermentables.usageNotes: Check for preservatives: potassium sorbate or benzoate will stop a ferment dead. Ascorbic acid is fine.

fermentables.name: Apple Juice Concentrate
fermentables.description: Roughly 68 Brix — about six times the strength of single-strength juice.
fermentables.usageNotes: Reconstitute at about 1 part concentrate to 5 parts water for a normal cider gravity.

fermentables.name: White Grape Juice
fermentables.description: Single-strength white must at harvest gravity — around 1.092 at 22 Brix.
fermentables.usageNotes: Commercial juice is usually already sulphited; wait 24 h before pitching.

fermentables.name: Red Grape Juice
fermentables.description: Single-strength red must. Juice alone carries little tannin — that comes from skin contact.
fermentables.usageNotes: For structure, ferment on skins or add grape tannin.

fermentables.name: Grape Juice Concentrate
fermentables.description: About 68 Brix. The standard body-and-sugar addition for kit wines and a common mead adjunct.
fermentables.usageNotes: Adds tartaric acid along with the sugar — account for it before making acid corrections.

fermentables.name: Orange Juice
fermentables.description: Ferments cleanly but loses most of its aroma; the result reads more like a dry citrus wine than orange juice.
fermentables.usageNotes: Pasteurised carton juice is reliable; check for added preservatives.

fermentables.name: Pineapple Juice
fermentables.description: Canned or carton juice is heat-treated, so the bromelain problem is already solved.
fermentables.usageNotes: Unlike fresh pineapple this will not attack gelatin or beer foam.

fermentables.name: Cranberry Juice (100%)
fermentables.description: Unsweetened cranberry juice is brutally acidic — most retail 'cranberry juice' is a sweetened cocktail at a fraction of the strength.
fermentables.usageNotes: Read the label: cocktail blends are typically 25% juice and already contain sugar.

fermentables.name: Tart Cherry Concentrate
fermentables.description: About 68 Brix, and the cheapest reliable route to genuine kriek character without sourcing fresh sour cherries.
fermentables.usageNotes: Add post-fermentation to preserve aroma. Roughly 1 L per 20 L batch gives a pronounced cherry note.
